seal.statement: During a critical spread cure the placement planner, from a direct census, retains or dispatches an ADD that takes a partition one voter over its replica target, and the receiving partition independently re-derives whether that overflow is allowed from its own priority-recovery view and may refuse the same transition; the owner decided on 2026-09-18 that replica-placement-cure-policy is the single authority for that overflow, that it authorizes one exact membership transition, and that the decision travels with the operation. Today nothing that says an ADD is a spread cure reaches the receiver: the move reason is never persisted. This quest builds the carrier and changes no decision. For exactly the priority over-target spread-cure condition the cure policy owner mints an authorization stating the intent critical_spread_cure, the desired replication factor read from the partition row's own authority, the membership publication epoch and voter count it observed, the authorized resulting voter count - the observed count plus one, never a blanket allowance - and the destination node; the coordinator completes it with the destination replica and the operation id and stamps it on the operation's existing first steps-history metadata record, with no schema change and no second record keyed off the operation; a binding owner decodes it as present, absent or malformed and never throws, and evaluates it against the receiving replica's own operation, node, replica, partition desired replication factor and current membership publication epoch; and the learner's count check, on every refusal and on its first passing check, states the decoded authorization, whether it would be honoured and why not, from the operation row it already read. An ADD for any other condition, a REPLACE and any operation on an ordinary partition carry no authorization. Every grant, deferral, refusal, reason, cap and scheduled recheck is identical to main's for every input, and a field absent from the move stays absent on the request and on the row.

text: Built the carrier: a new binding owner (spread-cure-transition-authorization.js) that decodes, evaluates and stamps one exact-transition authorization and never throws; authorizeSpreadCureTransition minted inside replica-placement-cure-policy.js from the partition row's own replication-target authority and the planning cycle's membership epoch threaded through calculateMoves; attachment at both cure call sites; the copy in applyCoordinatorOperationRequestMutationContext; the stamp in createOperationRecordInternal after the canonical replica id; the row decode in rowToOperation; one traversal at the learner yielding both the in-flight replica-id set and the owned operation row; the guard's payload states the decoded authorization, whether it would be honoured and why not. No decision changes.

Epoch-reader divergence (design section 9 item 3), MEASURED at f2fed102a: the planner reads getCurrentPublishedMembershipEpochSync -> readPublishedMembershipEpoch(planningSnapshot.publishedPlanningEpoch), which is the ACTIVE publication's epoch when its status is PUBLISHED and null otherwise (recovery-protocol-snapshot.js:659; published-membership-epoch-reading.js:24); the partition reads selectLatestPublishedMembershipEpoch over the cached control_plane_publications rows, which is the MAXIMUM epoch among PUBLISHED rows and 0 when there is none (membership-epoch-contract.js:300). They are two derivations of one fact and they diverge in two measured ways. (1) Unreadable: planner null, partition 0 - here the mint refuses to mint at all, so the direction is fail-closed. (2) Rows [PUBLISHED 6, PUBLISHED 7, ESTABLISHING 8] with the active publication at 6: planner 6, partition 7, so a valid authorization reads authorization_membership_generation_stale - a FALSE stale, not a false grant. No equality test was added, because the readers can diverge; pinning equality would pin something untrue. This gates the enforcing successor quest: under C2 a false stale becomes a refusal that no longer has the overflow budget behind it.

Over-target add-like inventory, started (precondition of the enforcing successor, not of this quest). VERIFIED by running the owners: only 5 of the 12 bootstrap-critical partitions can ever carry an authorization from this mint - schema_operations-p1, sql_transactions-p1, sql_transaction_participants-p1, sql_write_operations-p1, control_plane_publications-p1. replica_operations-p1, services-p1, nodes-p1, partitions-p1, message_groups-p1, tables-p1 and config-p1 are bootstrap-critical (isBootstrapCriticalSystemPartitionId, the guard's own critical branch) but NOT isNonLedgerPriorityPlacementCurePartition (the cure policy's gate), so authorizeSpreadCureTransition returns null for them by construction. The two owners do not use the same partition set. VERIFIED from code: classifyPriorityRecoveryFollowUpCureCondition returns UNHEALTHY_SOURCE_AT_TARGET (a REPLACE) whenever healthyReplicaCount >= targetReplicaCount, which INCLUDES the over-target case, and buildPriorityRecoveryMoveFields mints that move as a frozen literal that carries no authorization; its target learner on a critical partition over target is admitted today only by the overflow budget of 2. Production paths that can create an add-like operation at all (the only two production callers of rebalanceCoordinator.createOperation): unified-rebalancer-move-execution.js:309 for every planned move, and sql-query-engine-initial-partition-provisioning.js:430 for initial provisioning. INFERRED, not traced exhaustively: that the paired-relocation REPLACE cannot be minted while over target (the over-creation cap wipes the ADDs it would pair with), that plain under-representation ADDs cannot reach promotion over target, and that initial provisioning never runs for a bootstrap-critical partition.

Read-order delta, MEASURED. Main at f2fed102a already reads the in-flight add-like operation row's steps_history TWICE per check on a critical partition (normalizeReplicaOperationRecord and parsePriorityRecoveryStepsHistory inside buildPriorityRecoveryOperationContextFromRecord); the pinned MAIN_READ_ORDER got longer because an accessor made those existing reads visible, not because reads were added. With no authorization on the row - every row main writes today - the carrier's trace is main's order plus exactly one trailing memoised read:steps_history, and every cache read count is identical. With a PRESENT authorization the trace additionally gains filter:control_plane_publications and get:config, once: the partition's own published-epoch read via resolveLearnerPromotionMembershipEpoch, which runs ONLY when a record is actually present. That row class does not exist on main, so the sealed one-evaluation constraint's pinned order is met exactly; the lead and the verifier should confirm that the epoch read on an authorization-bearing row is the intended cost.

Deliberate strictening at the decode boundary, flagged for review: readSanctionedRecord requires authorizedResultingVoterCount === observedVoterCount + 1 exactly, not merely >= observedVoterCount as the design note's malformed table lists. That makes 'authorized above the exact transition' MALFORMED as well as 'authorized below observed'. It enforces the sealed statement's 'the observed count plus one, never a blanket allowance' at the boundary rather than trusting the mint, and it can only refuse, never grant. Also: decoding an unknown intent is MALFORMED (receipt 4), while evaluateSpreadCureTransitionAuthorization keeps its own authorization_intent_unknown row (receipt 5) as the fail-closed guard for a binding handed to it by any other route; the design note states intent in both tables and the two receipts require both.

round 1 REJECT (4 blocking). Confirmed green: planner, request and coordinator neutrality on real owners over 3000 seeded states (every plan, request, replica_operations INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE parameter list, final cache row, result, thrown error and logger line identical to main once the two new keys are stripped; rows without an authorization byte-identical; 69 of 1202 INSERTs carried the record, all 8 fields, only add:spread_replicas on the 5 eligible partitions); guard neutrality over 6000 seeded cases with 24 authorization variants and hostile loggers (0 differences); the mint reads the partition row's replication authority; no whole-move hash exists; the record survives complete/fail; statics green and the complexity tightening 1818 -> 1817 is real; 370 of 371 wide-net suites green. B1 the change turns test/rebalancer/replica-operation-membership-epoch-binding.test.js red (E8 single-decoder inventory: an unclassified reader of the membership epoch appeared in move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js); the binding module also validates the epoch with its own predicate beside the epoch binding owner. B2 decision-neutral / fail-closed-decode: for a PRESENT row the guard reads control_plane_publications and config inline as the logger argument, before the refusal is logged and the recheck scheduled; a faulting cache read there throws where main logs and schedules. B3 one-evaluation as sealed: a PRESENT row adds one whole-table publications read and one config get per payload-building check (12.8 -> 16.4 us at 8 publication rows, 32.8 at 200); main reads both zero times on the refusal path; 'that row class does not exist on main' rereads the constraint (R09). B4 R19: the production path planner -> request -> coordinator is unwitnessed - five mutants that disable or corrupt the carrier leave all eight receipts green (the loop threads no epoch: 0 minted moves in 1000 cases against 58; no row or epoch passed to the two cure sites; the request copy dropped; the request copy unconditional), and the sealed clause 'a field absent from the move stays absent on the request' has no witness. Non-blocking: the partition-row read runs on every plan for every entity type (message group with 3000 partition rows 5.5 -> 105 us per plan; main reads none); the decode scans every steps-history entry and the prototype chain, so 'first record' holds only by the writer; decode, evaluate, stamp and renderer throw on a Proxy, 2^53 passes the +1 check; an unnamed row targeting this node listed first makes the payload say absent although this learner's own row carries a record; an unreadable partition epoch reads 0 so any record is honoured and the stated fail-closed comment is false; observedVoterCount is max(in-flight accounting active count, active voter count), not a pure voter census; the src duplication tighten hint is an artefact of breaking the clone between rowToOperation and the second row decoder in replica-dispatch-readiness-capture.js, which now drift; calculateMoves(r, t, null) throws; nine surviving mutants incl. votersAfterPromotion swapped for the voter count and an operation-id mismatch that can never fire at the guard. Corrections to the implementer's findings: isBootstrapCriticalSystemPartitionId is true for all 45 system partitions at this head, 5 can mint, 40 cannot (not 5 of 12); the over-target unhealthy-source REPLACE is suppressed by its only caller when the inventory's active count exceeds the target, the residual risk being two different censuses; the [P6,P7,E8] epoch scenario does not reproduce - the planner's epoch is null while any newer publication is ESTABLISHING (no authorization is minted in that window) and the stale fence, evaluated at promotion time up to 60 s after planning, would read stale after every later join.

Lead ruling on B3 (the sealed one-evaluation constraint against the statement's epoch clause). The constraint stands as written: on no path does the guard read a table, row, snapshot or answer more often than main, for any row class. The statement's guard clause already says the count check states the authorization 'from the operation row it already read'. So the carry stage's guard does NOT read the partition's membership publication epoch: the binding owner's evaluation keeps the epoch criterion and its stale reason, proven at the owner level with a supplied epoch, and the guard supplies none and states that the epoch fence was not evaluated, as an explicit named outcome distinct from honoured and from refused. This also removes B2's unguarded read. It is the right call beyond the text: the owner directed on 2026-09-19 that the epoch disagreement is resolved at the authority boundary - one canonical interpretation for minting and validation, or a stable publication object resolved through one owner - so the carry stage must not bake in a guard-side reader that is about to be re-decided, and the verifier showed that fence would read stale after every later join. What the lab loses (live stale counts on refusals) moves to the overflow-budget audit, which characterises the readers on real owners.

CORRECTION, supersedes the 2026-09-19 inventory finding on this log ('5 of the 12 bootstrap-critical partitions'). VERIFIED on the staged tree with the verifier's partition-sets.mjs over INITIAL_PARTITION_IDS: isBootstrapCriticalSystemPartitionId is true for ALL 45 system partitions at this head, not 12. 5 can be minted for (schema_operations-p1, sql_transactions-p1, sql_transaction_participants-p1, sql_write_operations-p1, control_plane_publications-p1) and 40 cannot, because the cure policy's gate is isNonLedgerPriorityPlacementCurePartition while the promotion guard's critical branch is isBootstrapCriticalSystemPartitionId. No partition is mint-capable without being bootstrap-critical. The shape of the earlier finding stands - the two owners use different partition sets - but its magnitude was wrong by a factor of nearly four, and the enforcing successor must decide for 40 partitions, not 7.

CORRECTION, supersedes the priority-recovery REPLACE half of the 2026-09-19 inventory finding on this log. VERIFIED from code at unified-rebalancer-follow-up-move.js:641: buildPriorityRecoveryFollowUpMove returns OVER_REPLICATION_SUPPRESSED before it ever classifies a cure condition when inventory.accounting.activeCount > targetReplicaCount, so the over-target unhealthy-source REPLACE I reported cannot be minted by its only caller. The earlier finding read classifyPriorityRecoveryFollowUpCureCondition's '>=' without reading its caller's guard. The residual risk is narrower and real: the suppressor counts inventory.accounting.activeCount, while the over-creation cap counts max(activeCount, activeVoterCount) and the promotion guard counts its own voter census. A partition over target by VOTER count but not by ACTIVE count - the promotion window the planner's own comment at move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js documents, where a just-promoted voter still reads creating/syncing - passes the suppressor and can mint a follow-up REPLACE whose learner reaches the guard over target. Three censuses of one fact; that is what the enforcing successor's inventory must decide on, not the '>='.

CORRECTION, supersedes the 2026-09-19 epoch-reader finding on this log. VERIFIED on the staged tree with the verifier's epoch-divergence.mjs, which drives the REAL ControlPlaneReadinessService and MembershipPublicationCoordinatorReads rather than the pure functions I measured. My [PUBLISHED 6, PUBLISHED 7, ESTABLISHING 8] scenario does NOT reproduce: the planner reads null there, not 6, so no authorization is minted in that window at all. Measured over nine row sets: none -> planner null / partition 0; [P7] -> 7/7 agree; [P6,P7] -> 7/7 agree; [P6,P7,E8] -> null/7 NO MINT; [P7,E8] -> null/7 NO MINT; [P7, P8 excluding the planner node] -> null/8 NO MINT; [P7, ABANDONED 8] -> null/7 NO MINT; [P0] -> 0/0 agree. Two facts survive. (1) The planner's epoch is unreadable while ANY newer publication is ESTABLISHING or excludes the planning node, so the mint is silent in exactly the windows where a fence would matter - fail-closed, and it bounds how much this carrier can ever mint. (2) ONE row set still diverges: [P7 cluster_membership, P9 of another publication kind] gives planner 7, partition 9, a FALSE STALE, because the partition's selectLatestPublishedMembershipEpoch takes the maximum PUBLISHED epoch across ALL publication kinds while the planner's reader is kind-filtered. Since a promotion-time fence is evaluated up to 60 s after planning, it would also read stale after every later join. This is why the lead's ruling that the carry stage's guard reads no epoch is the right call and not merely a constraint reading.

For the overflow-budget audit quest, not for this one. VERIFIED from code: the observedVoterCount the mint states is evidence.voterReplicaCount, which the planner supplies as surplusVoterCount = Math.max(inFlightAccounting.activeCount, inFlightAccounting.activeVoterCount) (move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js). It is therefore not a pure voter census: a row that is ACTIVE by status but not a raft voter inflates it, and the authorized bound is observedVoterCount + 1, so the bound inflates with it. The cap takes the max deliberately (to stay non-regressive against the status-only read), but the authorization inherits that choice as a POLICY number the receiver will one day enforce against its own voter census. The two censuses disagree exactly in the promotion window the planner's own comment describes. Not acted on here: changing what the mint observes would change a decision, which this stage may not do.

Hole in the E8 single-decoder inventory, reported rather than exploited (lead's instruction). test/rebalancer/replica-operation-membership-epoch-binding.test.js gates on FIELD_TOKEN_PATTERN = /membershipPublicationEpoch|membership_publication_epoch|MEMBERSHIP_PUBLICATION_EPOCH/. The carrier moves the same durable epoch under the alias observedMembershipEpoch, which that pattern does not match, so six src files carry an epoch value the inventory cannot see: learner-promotion-count-check-evidence.js, partition-service-learner-promotion-wake-methods.js, move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js, move-planner-priority-spread-cure.js, replica-placement-cure-policy.js and spread-cure-transition-authorization.js. Two of those predate this quest (the wake methods' wake.observedMembershipEpoch, and the evidence renderer). I did NOT widen the pattern: widening it makes all six unclassified and pulls a pre-existing partition-side reader into an inventory owned by another quest. What I did instead: classified move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js as a pass-through (it reads planningContext.membershipPublicationEpoch and hands it on, with no coercion, predicate or zero-sentinel), and routed the authorization's own epoch-field validation through isBoundMembershipPublicationEpoch from the decode owner, so the epoch domain still has exactly one predicate. The guard's own remedy is for the inventory's owner to decide.

Round-2 repair of the four blocking findings and the eight must-fixes. B1: classified move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js as a pass-through in the E8 single-decoder inventory (it reads planningContext.membershipPublicationEpoch and hands it on untouched) and routed the authorization's own epoch-field validation through isBoundMembershipPublicationEpoch, so the epoch domain keeps one predicate; the inventory's token pattern does not see the observedMembershipEpoch alias and that hole is reported, not exploited. B2+B3 per the lead's ruling: the guard reads NO membership epoch on any path - the read is gone from the payload builder - and the binding owner's evaluation gains an explicit third outcome, membership_fence_not_evaluated, distinct from honoured and from refused, with its literal in the constants owner; the payload states partitionMembershipEpoch as the named not_read_by_the_carrier value, and wouldBeWithinAuthorizedBound is documented as arithmetic only. B4: a new production-path witness drives the real UnifiedRebalancer and RebalanceCoordinator end to end and kills all five carrier mutants; the expand cure site now re-states the authorization it re-types instead of carrying an earlier site's record past its own refusing mint. N1: the partition policy row is resolved lazily, at most once per plan and only after a cure condition holds, with a read-count witness against main's own measured per-plan reads. N2: the decode reads only steps_history[0] and only own data properties. N3: every entry point is total - decode, evaluate, stamp and mint - with safe-integer counts and exactness that rejects non-enumerable, symbol and class-instance shapes. N5a: a row naming this replica wins over an unnamed row targeting its node. N5b/N7/N8: the false unreadable-epoch comment and its branch are gone, rowToOperation's write-only exposure is removed, and a null planning context plans as main's two-argument call. N10: pinned with a 2000-case randomized differential against a verbatim copy of main's traversal, an owned-row selection table, a five-voter bound witness and a foreign-operation-id witness.

CORRECTION to my own round-1 report, not to a quest finding. I reported the src+scripts duplication tighten hint (57->56 clone groups, 1845->1807 lines) as pre-existing drift, reasoning that the baseline was last set on 2026-09-06 and that adding code cannot lower a duplicated-line count. That was an inference, and it was wrong. The verifier MEASURED main at f2fed102a: 57/57 and 1845/1845, with no hint. The hint was mine: the line I had inserted into rowToOperation broke the clone it shares with the second row decoder in src/control-plane/replica-dispatch-readiness-capture.js. N7 removes that line, which should restore the clone. The lesson is the one my own report should have applied: I had main's tree available and measured the row digests from it, and I did not measure this.

CORRECTION, supersedes the round-1 read-order finding on this log (entry 5) and extends the decode-strictening finding (entry 6). Entry 5 recorded that a PRESENT row costs one control_plane_publications read and one config read at the guard; that is no longer true of any row class. After the lead's B3 ruling the guard supplies no epoch at all, and the measured per-check read budget is now identical for a present, a malformed and an absent authorization: main's reads plus exactly ONE memoised steps_history parse of the row the in-flight add-like check had already read. The verifier's own 20-case guard-probe, re-run on the repaired tree, contains zero mentions of control_plane_publications or config, and its cases b1-b3 - a cache that faults on those tables - now return where they previously threw. Entry 6's strictening stands and grew: the counts are validated as SAFE integers (2**53 + 1 === 2**53, so a merely-integer check admitted an exact-transition that is a rounding artefact), the epoch field is validated by the epoch binding owner's own predicate rather than a second one, and exactness now rejects non-enumerable extras, Symbol extras and class instances as well as extra enumerable keys. Every entry point - decode, evaluate, stamp, mint and the log renderer - is total: the verifier's binding fuzz went from 58 throws to 0.

Round-2 neutrality, MEASURED on the verifier's own differentials against its existing main outputs at f2fed102a. End to end (e2e-harness, 3000 seeded cluster states, real UnifiedRebalancer and real RebalanceCoordinator): fieldDiffsAfterStrip is EMPTY - plans, requests, replica_operations SQL, logger lines, results, thrown errors and final rows are identical to main's once the two carrier keys are stripped. 78 of 3000 states carried an authorization (156 moves, 156 requests, 207 rows). Guard side (guard-harness, 6000 seeded cases with 24 authorization variants and hostile loggers): decisionDiffs count 0; traceNotSuperset is EMPTY and the whole traceDeltaHistogram is read:steps_history / read:stepsHistory entries only - no table read appears anywhere, so the carry stage reads no source main does not; threwCases are only the injected logger faults, matching main. One measured caveat, and the reason a witness was renamed: 237 of 3000 states show a partition-row read delta while only 78 carry an authorization. The lazy resolver is called when the CURE CONDITION holds, not when a record is minted, so 159 states pay one row read and mint nothing (an undeclared replication factor, an unreadable planning epoch). That is the instructed contract - read it only when a cure asks for it - but 'a plan that mints nothing costs main's reads' overstated it, so the witness now reads 'a plan that reaches no cure'.

round 2 APPROVE (0 blocking) on index tree c9b0ce91251b6851fc150733b5636707f521525f at f2fed102a; the wide net of 371 files ran green from a scratch commit of this exact tree (WIDENET_RC=0). The owner's four landing criteria, each stated to HOLD: (i) decision neutrality - planner, request and coordinator 0 differences over 3000 real end-to-end states (every plan, request, replica_operations INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE parameter list, final row, result, thrown error and logger line once the two keys are stripped), guard 0 differences over 6000 cases incl. 2069 hostile-logger cases and injected cache faults, the DECISION mutant dies; (ii) byte-identical rows without an authorization - every parameter list identical to main's, five frozen main digests pass, replica-operation-repository-row-methods.js byte-identical to main; (iii) minted from the partition row's declared replication authority - with the row declaring 5 against the planner's target 3 the record states 5, and an undeclared, zero, string or absent declaration mints nothing; (iv) no hidden new decision owner - the guard reads nothing main does not read (the whole read delta is one memoised steps_history parse; control_plane_publications and config are read 0 times; cost no longer depends on the publication table) and never states honoured (7217 payloads: outcome membership_fence_not_evaluated, honoured false), the evaluation has a single reader (the renderer), no planner, coordinator, dispatch or admission code reads the field, the epoch domain has one predicate, and the latent epoch comparison in the binding owner decides nothing in this stage. All four round-1 blockers repaired: the E8 epoch inventory is green and the planner file is truly a pass-through (coercion mutant dies); the three fault probes return exactly what main returns; the production-path witness through the real rebalance() and coordinator kills all five carrier mutants and witnesses 'absent stays absent'; the expand site's drop-and-re-mint is within the single-mint constraint and changes no plan (3000 of 3000 identical once the field is stripped). 54 verifier mutants: 51 killed, 3 equivalent or off-path survivors (the expand site keeping an identical record; a loosened predicate still caught by its sibling; the rebalancer-level calculateMoves wrapper, which has no src caller). Fuzz 0 throws (58 in round 1); decode confined to the first record and own data descriptors. Statics green, no duplication hint. Non-blocking, carried to the successor quest and the audit: the partition-row read could be later (the mint resolves the row before it checks the epoch: 159 of 237 reading states mint nothing); a stale renderer comment; the budget-planning wrapper edit is unnecessary; a supplied but invalid epoch reads not-evaluated rather than refused and a supplied 0 honours any record, so the successor must grant only on outcome honoured; a lying descriptor trap decodes PRESENT (unreachable from JSON rows; the stamp rejects every Proxy); PRESENT records' string fields are unbounded like main's own row echoes; evaluation ignores the row's type; observedVoterCount is max(active count, active voter count); the E8 inventory's token pattern misses the alias observedMembershipEpoch in six src files (two predate this quest) and must be settled before enforcement.

At land time the approved staged work was moved onto main 2a7606bcc by patch (main had advanced by records-only commits and by the lease-liveness-watermark-observed quest, whose files are disjoint from this quest's); the tree differs from the verified one only by main's own commits, the regenerated inventories, seal and shard classes, and the complexity ratchet's baseline, which now reads 1816 because both quests each removed one over-threshold function (the verified tree had 1818 -> 1817; main had meanwhile taken 1818 -> 1817 for the lease quest).
